rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec hike ~90% 25bp / ~10% 50bp (CME FedWatch); BoE Dec ~80%; ECB Dec ~90%; BoJ Dec ~84%; BoC Dec ~44%; RBA 4.85%, cut bets for 2027 building
rows.read: Fed Governor Christopher Waller argued for a half-point US hike in December unless the Fed signals another in January, and bets on a bigger step doubled. Weak Australian jobs figures point the other way there, supporting the view that Australian rates have peaked. US rates still look set to rise fastest, which keeps favouring the dollar.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: Australia employment Oct −43.5K (fcst +25.5K), unemployment 4.9% (fcst 4.7%); US housing starts Oct 1.309M, permits 1.295M; US jobless claims due 7:30 AM CT (fcst 198K)
rows.read: Australia lost jobs for a second month and unemployment hit a five-year high, the clearest sign yet that high rates are biting there. The US economy still looks firmer than most, which supports the dollar. Coming up: US weekly jobless claims.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: UK CPI Oct 3.6% y/y, core 2.8%; euro-area CPI Oct 4.0% final, core 2.6%; Japan core CPI Oct due 5:30 PM CT (fcst 2.3%)
rows.read: Inflation is still well above target almost everywhere, which keeps most central banks leaning toward hikes. Japan's inflation figures, out Thursday evening US time, will show whether the Bank of Japan has a clear case to hike in December.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: Houthi missile threat toward Riyadh caused damage (Nov 19); Hormuz crude flows near pre-war levels; USD/CHF ~0.8437; AUD/USD ~0.6695 (10-month low)
rows.read: A Houthi missile aimed at the Saudi capital caused damage overnight, yet markets stayed calm and the franc and yen drew no haven buying. With Gulf oil still flowing, interest rates are doing more to move currencies than the war. Weak Australian jobs added to pressure on the Aussie.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.figure: Brent ~$89.47, WTI ~$82.43 (steady overnight after −4% Wed); Hormuz flows near pre-war; gold ~$3,734 (dipped to ~$3,693)
rows.read: Oil steadied after a big drop as Gulf flows returned to normal, which keeps weighing on the Canadian dollar and helps energy buyers such as Japan and the euro area. Gold's slide to its lowest in more than a year weighs on the Aussie, since Australia is a big gold producer.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC report of Nov 10 (out late after Veterans Day): hedge funds for USD, GBP, AUD and gold; against EUR, NZD, CAD and CHF; slightly against JPY; real money disagrees on EUR, GBP and AUD
rows.read: The latest weekly figures show hedge funds leaning toward the dollar and the pound and against the euro, the kiwi and the Canadian dollar, with bets against the kiwi growing fastest. Big long-term investors take the other side on the euro, pound and Aussie. Where the two groups disagree, a surprise could set off a fast unwind.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: ECB FSR: France debt 119% of GDP, deficit 5.5%; US October deficit $404B, a record for the month; US 10-year ~5.07%
rows.read: France's debts, flagged by the European Central Bank as a risk, keep weighing on the euro. Record US government borrowing keeps long-term US borrowing costs near 5%, which weighs a little on trust in the dollar.
